..
An unsettled weather pattern produced by an extensive monsoon trough
dominated primarily by a developing disturbance known as Invest 93W 
well to the east, will continue for at least a few more days. Mostly
dry conditions are expected overnight, followed by some patchy 
showers developing Wednesday as the southwesterly monsoon continues
to build. Conditions will deteriorate as Invest 93W continues to 
consolidate and pass to the northeast of the Marianas sometime 
Friday through Saturday, inducing a significant monsoon surge that 
will bring a peak in shower and thunder potential by the weekend. 
Conditions are then expected to remain wet coming into next week as a
southwesterly monsoon regime continues.

Marine...
Combined seas of 3 to 4 feet will increase over the coming days, as 
Invest 93W continues to consolidate to the east of the Marianas and 
allows a southwesterly monsoon to return across the region toward the
weekend. As 93W passes to the northeast and a monsoon surge develops,
seas are expected to surpass 10 feet beginning Friday, likely 
becoming hazardous to small craft. A moderate risk of rip currents 
is expected to develop along east facing reefs of the Marianas 
beginning Wednesday, to then develop all reefs Wednesday night as a 
strengthening southwesterly swell envelops the region. There is some 
likelihood for hazardous surf to develop along south, west and north 
facing reefs of the Marianas by the weekend, highly dependent on the 
development of 93W and associated southwesterly monsoon surge.

Tropical Systems...
A developing disturbance found along the monsoon trough, Invest 93W,
is centered east of Saipan near 15.2N 155.5E. 93W is now rated 
medium by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), meaning that 
development into a significant tropical cyclone (tropical 
depression) is expected, but not within the next 24 hours. Invest 
93W continues to move slowly west-northwest. Convection has been 
persistent to the west through north of the center. Invest 93W is 
expected to slowly strengthen as it continues moving west-northwest 
to northwest over the coming days, likely passing north of Saipan 
late in the week. Residents of the Marianas, especially Tinian, 
Saipan and the northern CNMI, should monitor forecasts for any 
changes to expectations for Invest 93W.

For more information on Invest 93W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
Not much happening across eastern Micronesia this afternoon. Latest
guidance still showing a very dry pattern continuing for the next
several days across Pohnpei and Kosrae, with POPs (Probability of
Precipitation) remaining in the 10 percent range for Pohnpei and 20
percent for Kosrae. For Majuro, inflow and increased convergence due
to strengthening Invest 93W is still expected to bring increased
convection to the Marshalls beginning Wednesday night and continuing
through the weekend. No major changes were made to the marine
forecast.

Western Micronesia...
The monsoon trough remains the dominant feature effecting the 
region. The showers associated with this feature are over Palau and 
Yap, This feature is producing up to scattered and isolated 
thunderstorms, with the most active showers are northwest of Palau. 
As Invest 93W consolidates and moves west-northwest, the monsoon 
trough is north of the domain is expected to turn into a more NE-SW 
direction.

Palau is inbetween decaying showers produced by the convergences of
the monsoon trough and southwesterly winds, showers will vary 
between isolated and scattered through about Thursday as this
convergence shifts with 93W's consolidation. For the weekend, 
showers are expected to scattered as the monsoon surge passes over
the island. 

Today at Yap, showers of diminished over the island. Showers are
expected to build back in this evening and remain through the rest 
of the week as 93W consolidates and bring a monsoon surge over the 
island. Model guidance suggests up to 1 inch of rain each day through
the remainder of the week. Overall, a wet week is to be expected.

Chuuk is on the southern edge of the convective activity produced by
the monsoon trough. Here is where blow-off cloud cover is the 
greatest. This cloud cover is expected to produce isolated showers 
while the trough remains in a E-W orientation. Once 93W starts
pulling the trough away, drier conditions are expected to return
for the weekend and into next week.

Altimetry shows combined seas between 3 and 5 feet across the 
region. Winds will be light to moderate through Thursday, then winds 
are expected to build to gentle to fresh near the weekend. Sea 
conditions are expected to remain benign through Thursday, then seas
are anticipated to build to around 7 to 8 feet for the weekend and
beginning of next week.
